anomaly_def.Name: Optimizer Statistics Anomaly + Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly + Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly
anomaly_def.Description:
Optimizer Statistics Anomaly : Row-count and data-distribution metadata are stale, missing, or incomplete, causing systematic cardinality misestimation and sub-optimal plan selection.
Buffer Cache and Latch Contention Anomaly : Hot buffer pages and their protecting latches become serialization points, forcing sessions to spin or sleep while competing for page access or I/O slots.
Transaction Log Subsystem Anomaly : The write-ahead logging path (log buffer, log file, flush, switch, or archive) cannot keep up with redo generation, lengthening commit latency and back-pressuring writers.

When all three root causes coexist, the database exhibits intertwined symptoms: queries choose inefficient plans that inadvertently hammer a small set of index or data pages, sharply increasing buffer hit traffic and latch waits; the resulting page churn produces a surge of dirty buffers whose flushes queue behind an already saturated transaction log, inflating log-flush and checkpoint waits. End users observe erratic response times, spikes in CPU spin, blocked commits, and sudden throughput collapses after data-modification bursts or bulk-load events. Execution-plan explain outputs show severe cardinality errors, while performance views simultaneously record high buffer busy/latch contention and log-related waits, making the dominant bottleneck difficult to isolate.

Causally, stale or missing statistics drive the optimizer toward plans that concentrate reads or inserts on a few root/leaf pages or hot ranges, amplifying latch contention in the buffer pool. The repeated retries and page splits from this contention generate excess redo, which in turn overwhelms the transaction-log subsystem and delays buffer flush completion. The slowed log flush prolongs page-write hold times, further intensifying latch pressure and starving the buffer cache of free pages, which increases page eviction and reload cycles. This feedback loop magnifies latency and stalls across the stack, turning three individually manageable issues into a cascading performance collapse during write-intensive OLTP workloads.

entry.official_description: invalid row count in limit clause
entry.cause_analysis: The failure is typically associated with a general engine-level execution problem surfaced by the official error catalogue, but its precise trigger must be interpreted together with workload context and surrounding evidence.
entry.solution_guidance: Review the surrounding workload, official description, and engine state to determine whether the issue is rooted in SQL logic, resource pressure, configuration, or environmental instability.
